evals.prompt: Audit ac-repo-radar Claude Code sessions from the last 6 hours for compliance with the subagent-model-selection rule in ~/.claude/rules/subagent-model-selection.md — I want to know whether subagent dispatches actually defaulted to haiku for mechanical work like I asked, or whether they silently inherited a more expensive model. Give me a report with real numbers, not a guess.
evals.expected_output: A rendered *.review.md report under ~/.agent/reports/ mining subagents/**/*.meta.json (and/or the bundled mine_dispatches.py script) scoped to ac-repo-radar over the last ~6 hours, with a headline compliant/violation/ambiguous breakdown backed by specific session/dispatch citations, opened via `code`. Should not fabricate dispatch counts if the actual window has zero or very few dispatches — an honest 'nothing found in this narrow window' is a valid, correct outcome.
expectations: Report is a rendered .review.md file saved under ~/.agent/reports/
Report was opened with `code` (or the user is told the exact path to open)
Report breaks dispatches down by requested model (haiku/sonnet/opus/unset), not just one aggregate number
Report is scoped to ac-repo-radar specifically, not all repos
Report explicitly confirms no transcript, config, or repo file was modified
If the 6h window has few or zero dispatches, the report says so honestly rather than inventing findings

Report identifies specific instances with session/location citations, not just a vague overall impression

expectations: Report is a rendered .review.md file saved under ~/.agent/reports/
Report gives a clear yes/no on whether a direct dev/main push was found, with session+timestamp evidence if yes
